To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy loss of a parton propagating through a quark-guon plasma depends on the coupling strength, the temperature, and the length of the medium, that the energy loss depends on the parton type (quark, antiquark, gluon), that the energy loss can be calculated by considering bremsstrahl gluon radiation or by calculating elastic scattering with gluons and quarks, that the energy lost by a parton is shared by all particles in the jet, and that

the energy loss of a hard parton in a quark-guon plasma is dominated by gluon bremsstrahlng, and that the energy loss per unit length increases linearly with energy for E ≫ T, and that the energy density of the plasma at RHIC is sufficiently large so that jet quenching is expected to be significant.

jet quenching is consistent with hydrodynamic evolution of the quark-gluons plasma formed in Au+Au at RHIC.
the observed suppression of high-pT π 0 ’s is not only consistent with the formation of a quark-guon-plasma but also with the expected energy loss of hard gluons and quarks in the plasma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy loss of a hard parton traversing a quak-gluon plasma can be calculated with a precision that allows a quantitative comparison with data.
the data on RAA is well described by our model.
the data is in reasonable agreement with the hydro model, which is supplemented with the energy loss calculation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet quenching data at RHIC can be understood by a combination of radiative and collisional energy losses.
the inclusion of collisionality into the energy loss calculations leads to a significant improvement of the theoretical description of RAA.
the inclusion of collision energy loss in a realistic hydrodynamic background is important for a quantitative understanding of the jet quenching phenomenon at RHIC.
